summary: The Australian Government Research Training Program (RTP) gives Australian universities block funding that they use to support research students in research doctorates and research Master's degrees, both Australian and international. There is no single national application: you apply to the university, which decides who gets an RTP place, how much and on what terms. The support can include a tuition fee offset, a living-cost stipend and allowances for research costs, as the universities I read describe below.
eligibility_notes:
National level: the Government describes the RTP as supporting domestic and international students in a research doctorate or a research Master's; students apply directly to a participating university and each university sets its own selection. The Department of Education's own pages could not be opened during this check, so the points above on national rules are carried over from stored data and from the Study Australia page.

University examples I read. An overseas (international) candidate must be enrolled in an accredited higher degree by research (HDR) course at an Australian university (UQ policy). Selection is on academic merit and research potential, ranked competitively (ANU, UQ, Flinders). At ANU the award also depends on confirmed supervisors and available space and resources and fit with ANU research strategy. At UQ you must be nominated by the school or institute where you will enrol and be assessed as meeting all admission conditions; a school can nominate at most 8 international applicants per round. At Flinders, a stipend holder may not take other income for general living costs above 75% of the stipend rate, and a person is ineligible if they already hold a research doctorate, seek a second Master's, or hold a duplicating award or paid study leave; people who previously held an Australian Government RTP stipend, an Australian Postgraduate Award or a similar award are excluded unless it ended within six months. UQ does not accept applicants who are readmitted to a previous UQ HDR programme or who study remotely from outside Australia.

Language and other requirements: English proficiency evidence is part of the UQ expression of interest, and ANU ranks applicants partly on English competence. Requirements for an international student's visa, English test score and entry grades are set by each university.
age_experience_notes: No age limit or work experience rule found on the pages I read. At ANU a separate university research scholarship asks for at least an Honours H1 or equivalent; the RTP stipend page itself says ranked on merit.
funding_summary: What you can get depends on the university. The universities I read describe three parts: a tuition fee offset (ANU offers an RTP International Fee Offset Scholarship, UQ lists tuition fees as covered, and Flinders gives the offset to international students who hold the RTP stipend), a tax-free living stipend paid fortnightly or on the university's schedule, and allowances such as relocation, thesis costs, a dependent child allowance (ANU, international students) and paid leave. Length: ANU stipend 3.5 years with a 6-month extension available; ANU fee offset 4 years for a PhD and 2 years for an MPhil; UQ 3.5 years with a possible one-year extension; Flinders doctorate up to 3 years (up to 6 months more with approval) and research Master's up to 2 years.
programmes_note: Research doctorate and research Master's (higher degree by research) only; coursework degrees and higher doctorates are not covered. Any field offered by the university can be considered; universities link awards to supervisor availability and research strengths.
institutions_note: Only Australian higher education providers that receive RTP block funding. Each runs its own competitive rounds and application route, so check each university's page. The Government keeps a list of providers eligible for the funding, which I could not open.

summary.detail: Research Master's (for example Master of Philosophy). Flinders: stipend up to 2 years with no extension; fee offset 1 to 2 years full time. ANU: fee offset 2 years for an MPhil; stipend page for the ANU University Research Scholarship gives 1.5 years for MPhil. A second Master's is not funded at Flinders.
summary.source_text: Masters: up to 2 years, with no extension

summary.detail: Research doctorate (PhD). ANU stipend 3.5 years (6-month extension available); ANU fee offset 4 years; UQ 3.5 years with a possible one-year extension; Flinders stipend up to 3 years plus up to 6 months with approval, fee offset 3 to 4 years full time.

benefits.limit_text: Tuition fee offset, when the university offers it: ANU International Fee Offset (4 years PhD, 2 years MPhil); UQ lists tuition fees as covered; Flinders for international students who hold the RTP stipend
benefits.conditions: Paid by the Government and the university to the university, not to the student. Flinders: international students are eligible if they hold the RTP stipend. Exceeding the funded period means the student pays international tuition.

benefits.limit_text: Living stipend, when awarded: ANU 2027 full-time base AUD 40,475 a year; UQ 2026 AUD 39,220 a year tax free; Flinders 2025 full-time AUD 35,010 a year tax free
benefits.conditions: Rates are set by each university and indexed each year. Stored national figures (carried over from stored data, not re-read): 2027 base AUD 35,550 and maximum AUD 55,537. Flinders part-time rate is half the full-time rate. Stipend holders must keep to study conditions and limits on other income.

benefits.limit_text: Overseas Student Health Cover: single cover included at UQ; ANU reimburses OSHC for international recipients through the fee offset
benefits.conditions: Depends on the university. ANU says the OSHC reimbursement covers you and your immediate family.

benefits.limit_text: Travel and removal allowance for moving to Canberra (ANU); relocation allowance up to AUD 1,485 for stipend holders moving from overseas or interstate (Flinders)
benefits.conditions: Flinders: adult AUD 505, child AUD 255, plus economy or student concession airfares. Not mentioned at UQ on the page read.

benefits.limit_text: Thesis allowance (ANU; Flinders AUD 500 with receipts), dependent child allowance for international students (ANU), paid medical, maternity and parental leave (ANU), recreation and sick leave (Flinders)
benefits.conditions: Allowances for the ancillary costs of a research degree are decided by each university.

benefits.limit_text: No separate housing payment found on the pages read
benefits.conditions: Housing costs come from the stipend.

requirements.text: Application for admission to the higher degree by research programme. At ANU you tick the option for other scholarships on the admission form and no separate scholarship application is needed. UQ asks first for an expression of interest, then a full application once your chosen advisor supports it. Flinders uses an electronic scholarship application in its international round.
Academic transcripts and degree certificates for previous qualifications.
requirements.conditional_rule: Listed on the UQ expression of interest
Listed on the UQ expression of interest

requirements.text: Referee reports. At ANU referee reports are requested automatically when you submit and must arrive before the deadline; the page suggests submitting 2 to 3 weeks early. UQ asks for referee details in the expression of interest.
English language proficiency information. The exact test and score are set by each university.
Name of a proposed advisor or supervisor and agreement to supervise (UQ expression of interest; ANU encourages contacting the HDR convener or a prospective supervisor before applying).

application_steps.title: Choose a university, research topic and supervisor
application_steps.detail: RTP is not applied for centrally: you pick a participating university, find a research area and a prospective supervisor or advisor, and follow that university's route. ANU encourages you to contact the HDR convener or a possible supervisor first. UQ's first step is to find an advisor with the right expertise.

application_steps.title: Apply for admission and the scholarship at the university
application_steps.detail: ANU: select the 'ANU - Other Scholarship' option on the HDR admission application; no separate application. UQ: submit an expression of interest, then a full application after the advisor supports it; the full application must be complete, documented, supported by the advisor and endorsed by the enrolling unit. Flinders: electronic application in a round called around June for international students and closing around August.

application_steps.title: Meet the university's round deadlines
application_steps.detail: ANU international: Round 1 deadline 31 August for commencement the next year; Round 2 deadline 15 April for same-year start. UQ 2027 rounds close 25 January 2027, 31 May 2027 and 4 October 2027, and the international round for later 2027 or early 2028 start closed on 19 October 2026. Other universities set their own dates.

application_steps.title: Competitive ranking by a university committee
application_steps.detail: A committee ranks eligible applicants on academic performance, research capability and research potential, project quality, supervisor and research environment, and referee reports. At UQ the Dean of the Graduate Research School chairs the selection committee. At Flinders the HDR Scholarships Committee ranks on merit and research potential and gives priority to first-time doctoral students. ANU funds the top-ranked candidates, subject to supervisor, space and resources.

application_steps.title: Outcome
application_steps.detail: Outcome timing depends on the round. For example UQ lists outcomes from 6 April 2027 (round 1), 10 August 2027 (round 2) and 14 December 2027 (round 3); the international round that closed on 19 October 2026 has outcomes from 22 February 2027.

application_steps.title: Accept, enrol and start the research degree
application_steps.detail: Recipients must formally accept, be enrolled and stay enrolled while they hold the award. Flinders requires a start date no later than 31 March (30 June in exceptional cases).

application_steps.title: Keep to the award conditions
application_steps.detail: Support continues with satisfactory academic progress. Typical rules from the universities I read: study full time (30 to 40 hours a week at Flinders), limits on outside income for stipend holders, approval needed for intermission, leave rules, and the award ends when the maximum period is reached, the thesis is submitted, or the student stops meeting eligibility or commits misconduct.

fetch_problems: education.gov.au (Research Training Program page, student FAQ and list of eligible providers) timed out on repeated tries, so the national rules and rates were not re-read. The stored national figures are carried over and marked.
Griffith University RTP pages returned HTTP 403.
The legislation register page for the guidelines that govern the RTP was not usable (the search result said the 2017 guidelines have been replaced; I could not open the replacement).
notes: National stipend figures AUD 35,550 (base) and AUD 55,537 (maximum) for 2027 are carried over from stored data. They conflict with ANU's 2027 base of AUD 40,475 and UQ's 2026 figure of AUD 39,220, so the universities appear to pay above the national base, or the stored figures are for a different measure. Editors should confirm on the Department's page.
Flinders rates and rules are on an administrative page whose rates are 2025; use only as an example of the type of rules.
This scholarship is a funding stream, not a single named award; students cannot apply 'to the RTP'.
